titleStmt.title: Intelligence Memorandum Prepared in the Central Intelligence Agency

div.head: 467. Intelligence Memorandum Prepared in the Central Intelligence Agency

p.hi: Venezuela-Latin America: Reaching for a Unified Foreign Policy

div.p: Venezuela’s continuing attempts to convene a foreign ministers’ meeting with Brazil, Argentina, and Mexico—proposed as the first step toward formulating a coordinated foreign policy—reflect the Herrera administration’s concern over what it perceives as the East-West thrust of the emerging US policy for Latin America. Fearing that the region could become the setting for bipolar conflict, Caracas is trying to focus and project Latin American uneasiness before Washington settles on its course.

The four nations, however, hold widely divergent political views and pursue some dissimilar goals. Although they share the region’s general uneasiness over the potential effect of superpower interference on security interests and economic development, their differences—at any multilateral meeting—would color discussions of Central America, Cuba, and US policy.

Thus, on balance, talks among the four would offer a forum for reiterating traditional Latin American positions on nonintervention and self-determination—positions that, while couched in global terms, would be directed primarily at the United States. But on the issues fundamental to a unified foreign policy, a meeting is likely to be more revealing in underscoring regional disharmony than in establishing bases from which to proceed.
[Omitted here is the body of the memorandum.]

note.p: Source: Central Intelligence Agency, Office of Support Services (DI), Job 82T00565R: Production Case Files (1981), Box 1, Folder 23: Venezuela—Latin America: Reaching For a Unified Foreign Policy. Secret; Noforn; [handling restriction not declassified]. Prepared in the Office of Political Analysis and coordinated with DO, the Office of Economic Research, and the NIO for Latin America. Information available as of July 16 was used in the preparation of the memorandum.
